summary: Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Davis, and served as a Research Group Leader in the Department of Religious Diversity at the Max Planck Institute.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who studied at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and completed his Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen. He has held professorships at Copenhagen and Oxford, and served as Leiter of the Center for Subjectivity Research.

Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar Daniel A. Getz completed his PhD at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. Attested in 2019 as an associate professor at Bradley University, he also studied under Ying-shih Yü, Masaaki Chikusa, and Taryo Makita.

Daniel Aitken specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania under doctoral supervisor Jay L. Garfield, and also studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He held assistant professor posts at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996-2003).

Daniel Baum is a linguist and Indologist who earned his BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and his doctorate at Leiden University (circa 2001-2006) under Alexander Lubotsky. He also studied under Saul Migron.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in Japanology and history and archaeology. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under MA supervisor Akiko Walley, attested in 2014.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Indiana University and earned his doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, later serving as associate professor at Cornell University (attested 2000-2008).

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned degrees from Yale University and Harvard University, and took up a post at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale, president of the University of California, founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875-1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution and the American Oriental Society.

Daniel Cozort works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, taught briefly at Bates College, and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Dickinson College (~1988-2020).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. From approximately 1993 to 2015, he held posts as director of research at the CNRS and Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his AB at Harvard, studying under Walter Eugene Clark and Kalipada Tarkacharya. He spent his career at Harvard (~1951-1983), serving as Wales Professor of Sanskrit.

Daniel John Gogerly was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He directed the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818-1834), chaired the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (1838), and served as officer and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1858-1862).

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a longtime professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973-2001).

Daniel M. Stuart is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. Attested in 2017, he served as Assistant Professor of South Asian and Buddhist Studies at the University of South Carolina.
Daniel P. Brown specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Ngawang Wangyal. He served as a professor at Harvard University from approximately 1983 until 2022.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he was advised by Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1923-1925), succeeded Joseph Hackin, and later held a post at Princeton University.
